arxiv-2005-06921.title: On the Performance Analysis of Streaming Codes over the Gilbert-Elliott Channel
arxiv-2005-06921.creator: Myna Vajha, Vinayak Ramkumar, Mayank Jhamtani, P. Vijay Kumar
arxiv-2005-06921.description: Abstract The Gilbert-Elliot (GE) channel is a commonly-accepted model for packet erasures in networks. Streaming codes are a class of packet-level erasure codes designed to provide reliable communication over the GE channel. The design of a streaming code may be viewed as a two-step process.

arxiv-2210-15091.title: Segmentation of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions across Hospitals: Learn Continually or Train from Scratch?
arxiv-2210-15091.creator: Enamundram Naga Karthik, Anne Kerbrat, Pierre Labauge, Tobias Granberg, Jason Talbott, Daniel S. Reich, Massimo Filippi, Rohit Bakshi, Virginie Callot, Sarath Chandar, Julien Cohen-Adad
arxiv-2210-15091.description: Abstract Segmentation of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) lesions is a challenging problem. Several deep-learning-based methods have been proposed in recent years. However, most methods tend to be static , that is, a single model trained on a large, specialized dataset, which does not generalize well.

arxiv-2301-08887.title: Observational imprints of enhanced scalar power on small scales in ultra slow roll inflation and associated non-Gaussianities
arxiv-2301-08887.creator: H. V. Ragavendra, L. Sriramkumar, Chennai 600 036, India. E-mail: sriram@physics.iitm.ac.in
arxiv-2301-08887.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by H. V. Ragavendra, L. Sriramkumar, Chennai 600 036, India. E-mail: sriram@physics.iitm.ac.in. The discovery of gravitational waves from merging binary black holes has generated considerable interest in examining whether these black holes could have a primordial origin.

arxiv-2305-15867.title: Extracting Text Representations for Terms and Phrases in Technical Domains
arxiv-2305-15867.creator: Francesco FuscoIBM Research ffu@zurich.ibm.com, Diego AntogniniIBM Research Diego.Antognini@ibm.com
arxiv-2305-15867.description: Abstract Extracting dense representations for terms and phrases is a task of great importance for knowledge discovery platforms targeting highly-technical fields. Dense representations are used as features for downstream components and have multiple applications ranging from ranking results in search to summarization.

arxiv-2307-03747.title: The backreaction effect of sound speed resonance in DBI inflation.
arxiv-2307-03747.creator: Bichu Li, Chao Chen, Bo Wang
arxiv-2307-03747.description: Abstract We examine the backreaction effect of the enhanced small-scale scalar perturbations from the sound speed resonance (SSR) mechanism for primordial black hole formation in Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) inflation Within the perturbative regime, the backreaction effect of perturbations on the background dynamics can be described by an effective action after integrating out the perturbation sector.

arxiv-2504-07346.title: When Koopman Meets Hamilton and Jacobi
arxiv-2504-07346.creator: Umesh Vaidya, IEEE Senior Member
arxiv-2504-07346.description: Abstract In this paper, we establish a connection between the spectral theory of the Koopman operator and the solution of the Hamilton Jacobi (HJ) equation. The HJ equation occupies a central place in systems theory, and its solution is of interest in various control problems, including optimal control, robust control, and input-output analysis.

arxiv-2506-17635.title: Entropy decrease and emergence of order in collective dynamics Thanks: I thank Thomas Chen for helpful discussions. arxiv-2506-17635.creator: Eitan Tadmor
arxiv-2506-17635.description: Abstract . We study the hydrodynamic description of collective dynamics driven by velocity alignment . It is known that such Euler alignment systems must flock towards a limiting “flocking” velocity, provided their solutions remain globally smooth. To address this question of global existence we proceed in two steps. (i) Entropy and closure.

arxiv-2507-23695.title: On the Achievable Rate of Satellite Quantum Communication Channel using Deep Autoencoder Gaussian Mixture Model
arxiv-2507-23695.creator: Mouli Chakraborty 1 , Subhash Chandra 1 , Avishek Nag 3 , Anshu Mukherjee 2 4
arxiv-2507-23695.description: Abstract We present a comparative study GMM ( GMM ) and DAGMM ( DAGMM ) for estimating satellite quantum channel capacity, considering HQN ( HQN ) and transmission constraints. While GMM is simple and interpretable, DAGMM better captures non-linear variations and noise distributions. Simulations show that DAGMM provides tighter capacity bounds and improved clustering.

pmc-10647503.title: An Interpretable Radiomics Model Based on Two-Dimensional Shear Wave Elastography for Predicting Symptomatic Post-Hepatectomy Liver Failure in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma
pmc-10647503.creator: Xian Zhong, Zohaib Salahuddin, Yi Chen, Henry C. Woodruff, Haiyi Long, Jianyun Peng, Xiaoyan Xie, Manxia Lin, Philippe Lambin
pmc-10647503.description: Simple SummaryTwo-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) has demonstrated predictive value for symptomatic post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Our aim was to develop and validate an interpretable radiomics model based on 2D-SWE for predicting symptomatic PHLF in patients undergoing liver resection for HCC.

pmc-10879885.title: Échec de la campagne d’éradication de la poliomyélite avec le vaccin oral: on ne vaccine pas sans adhésion
pmc-10879885.creator: Bernard SEYTRE
pmc-10879885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). RésuméTrente-cinq ans après son lancement, l'Initiative mondiale pour l’éradication de la poliomyélite n'a toujours pas atteint son but, originellement fixé à l'an 2000. Non seulement le virus sauvage de type 1 de la poliomyélite est toujours endémique dans deux pays, mais une nouvelle épidémie due à des virus dérivés du virus vivant atténué utilisé pour le vaccin oral se propage depuis 2016.

pmc-11410867.title: Gender disparities among prestigious biomedical award recipients in Japan: A cross sectional study
pmc-11410867.creator: Hayase Hakariya, Tatsuki Ikejiri, Arisa Hakariya, Mayumi Hara
pmc-11410867.description: fessional awards. 8 , 9 The gender gap has been observed in the number of original papers, 7 , 10 which is an important indicator for evaluating performance, and the proportion of women first author is lower in women scientists.

pmc-11590837.creator: Ambre Sauvage, Emeline Laurent, Bruno Giraudeau, Marc-Florent Tassi, Lucile Godillon, Leslie Grammatico-Guillon, Clarisse Dibao-Dina
pmc-11590837.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesThe first COVID-19 lockdown raised concerns about reduced access to primary care, especially for people with chronic diseases particularly at risk in the absence of follow-up. However, the COVIQuest trial, evaluating the impact of a general practitioner (GP) phone call (intervention) to chronic patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) or mental health disorder (MHD) concluded that the intervention had no effect at 1 month on the rate of self-reported hospitalisations in the CVD subtrial, whereas the intervention group in MHD subtrial might have

pmc-11710321.title: Aβ immunotherapy drives immune activation and cerebrovascular damage in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11710321.creator: Xavier Taylor, Harun Noristani, Griffin Fitzgerald, Herold Oluoch, Nick Babb, Tyler McGathey, Justin T Hole, Pascale Lacor, Ronald B DeMattos, Yaming Wang, Neuroscience Discovery, Lilly Research Laboratories, Eli Lilly and Company, Indianapolis, IN, 46285, USA
pmc-11710321.description: BackgroundAnti‐amyloid‐β (Aβ) immunotherapy trials have shown amyloid‐related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) as the most common and serious adverse events linked to pathological changes in cerebral vasculature. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying how amyloid immunotherapy triggers vascular damage, increases vascular permeability, and results in microhemorrhages remains unclear.

pmc-12473795.title: Selenium Nanoparticles: Synthesis, Stability and In Vitro Evaluation in Human Lens Epithelial Cells
pmc-12473795.creator: Lulwah Al-Bassam, Mohammed M Naiyer, Christopher J Morris, Steve Brocchini, Gareth R Williams, Donato Cosco
pmc-12473795.description: Background/Objectives: Oxidative stress plays a critical role in the development of ocular diseases such as cataracts. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) offer antioxidant benefits with low toxicity. This study aimed to evaluate the antioxidant activity of SeNPs coated with D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS) in human lens epithelial (HLE) cells.

pmc-12526844.title: Epidemiology and Outcomes of Peptic Ulcer Perforation: An Analytical Cross-Sectional Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in India
pmc-12526844.creator: Ujala Murmu, Zenith Kerketta, Khushboo Rani, Krishna Murari, Anish Baxla, Sunny, Neyaz Ahmad, Amit Nishant, Shreya, Ajay Soreng
pmc-12526844.description: BackgroundPeptic ulcer perforation (PUP) is a life-threatening complication of peptic ulcer disease (PUD), with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low-resource settings. Driven by factors such as Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) use, and socio-economic disparities, PUP requires urgent surgical intervention.

pmc-12609019.title: Energy Drink Knowledge, Consumption, and Regulation Support Among Polish Medical and Non-Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12609019.creator: Paulina Mularczyk-Tomczewska, Tytus Koweszko, Julia Koperdowska, Ewelina Adamska, Andrzej Silczuk
pmc-12609019.description: Background: Energy drink [ED] consumption is common among young adults and has been linked to adverse health effects and risky behaviors. This study compared medical and non-medical university students to assess whether health education influences knowledge, consumption, and attitudes toward EDs.

pmc-12663367.title: Effect of mixed fermentation of Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Lactobacillus helveticus, Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus on physicochemical and flavor characteristics of pumpkin juice
pmc-12663367.creator: Ren-qin Tan, Chun-li Zhou, Man-jun Zhang, Wei Su, Shao-fang Liu, Le-yi Yao, Wen-hui Pan, Wen Li
pmc-12663367.description: Probiotic fermentation with a defined consortium (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Lactobacillus helveticus, and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus) successfully transformed pumpkin juice into a functional beverage with enhanced bioactivity and appealing aroma. The fermented product achieved a high viable count of 7.37 log CFU mL−1, along with significant increases in vitamin C, total phenolics, flavonoids, and carotenoids compared to unfermented juice.

pmc-13019242.title: Chemosensitizer Effects of Coencapsulation of Curcumin and Cabazitaxel in Nanostructured Lipid Carriers in Glioblastoma Cells
pmc-13019242.creator: Franciely Rufino de Almeida Lima, Hélder A. Santos, Priscyla D. Marcato
pmc-13019242.description: Gliomas are the most common primary tumors of the central nervous system and are associated with poor prognosis. Current therapy with Temozolomide shows limited efficacy, highlighting the need for new treatment options. Cabazitaxel (CBZ), a chemotherapeutic agent approved for prostate cancer, has shown efficacy in preclinical glioblastoma models.

pmc-13049056.title: Understanding college student’s continued intention in choirs through music quality and psychosocial influences
pmc-13049056.creator: Yingze Yue, Pu Qu
pmc-13049056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigates the motivational factors influencing college student’s continued participation in choirs, focusing on the effects of music quality and psychosocial factors on their sustained learning intentions within the context of Chinese higher education. While choirs are widely recognized for enhancing teamwork and emotional communication, there is a lack of in-depth research on student’s expectations before joining choirs and their commitment to ongoing participation in collectivist cultural settings.

pmc-13072542.title: Characterization of a Pasteurella multocida type A strain associated with a severe bronchopneumonia outbreak in gilts
pmc-13072542.creator: Sophie Kähl, Helene Fenzl, Martin Dembowski, Regina Kröger, Claudia Hartig, Carla Heddier, Reiner Ulrich, Johannes Kauffold, Christoph Georg Baums
pmc-13072542.description: BackgroundIn pigs, Pasteurella multocida (P. multocida) serotypes A, B and D are causative agents of pneumonia, hemorrhagic septicemia and progressive rhinitis atrophicans, respectively. In the case of bronchopneumonia in pigs, P. multocida is generally regarded as an opportunistic pathogen following predisposing infectious agents. This study was initiated by an outbreak of bronchopneumonia in gilts associated with high mortality during lactation.

pmc-13161963.title: Femoral Nerve Paralysis Associated with Traumatic Iliacus Hematoma: A Case Report
pmc-13161963.creator: Hiroki Kobayashi, Keisuke Horiuchi
pmc-13161963.description: Introduction:We report a case of femoral nerve paralysis associated with a traumatic iliacus hematoma.Case Report:A 19-year-old female presented with left groin pain. She fell from a height of 3 m during cheerleading and experienced numbness in the left femoral nerve region along with quadriceps muscle weakness.

pmc-13204358.title: In Vitro Effects of Minor Olive Oil Compounds on Prostacyclin/Thromboxane Balance Under Acute High-Glucose Conditions
pmc-13204358.creator: Ana María Sánchez-Tévar, Laura Ortega-Hombrados, María Dolores Rodríguez-Pérez, María Monsalud Arrebola-Ramírez, Esther Martín-Aurioles, Sergio Pérez-Burillo, Cristina Verdugo-Cabello, Rocío Cobos-López, José Pedro De La Cruz, José Antonio González-Correa
pmc-13204358.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of several minor components of extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) on platelet thromboxane and vascular prostacyclin production in rat aortic rings under high-glucose conditions (300 mg/dL), in relation to their potential antioxidant actions. Under hyperglycaemic conditions, thromboxane production was 1.3 times higher, while prostacyclin production was 40.

pmc-13325154.title: Unraveling the Impacts of Preprocessing on the Metabolite Profile of Bitter Almond Using UPLC-MS/MS and GC–MS Analysis
pmc-13325154.creator: Liwei Zhao, Jianlong Ma, Fengxia Hao, Xuebin Li, Qingqi Feng

pmc-13400882.title: Lappaconitine hydrobromide prevents NLRP3-GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis to alleviate sepsis-induced acute lung injury by enhancing NR1H3
pmc-13400882.creator: Yuejia Lan, Qingrui Zhong, Hongkai Huang, Xiao Deng, Lu Yang, Jiayi Sun, Mingyang Liu, Xianli Meng, Jiasi Wu
pmc-13400882.description: Evidence indicates that nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group H member 3 (NR1H3) activation mitigates sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SALI) by reducing inflammatory response. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying NR1H3-inflammation interactions in addressing SALI remain unclear. Moreover, limited phytochemicals have been documented to ameliorate SALI via this pathway.

pmc-13520843.title: Returning home and re-negotiating mental health: a qualitative study of help-seeking, stigma, and cultural identity among Algerian international student returnees
pmc-13520843.creator: Nesrine Boussaoui, Stephen Kelly, Nicola Cogan
pmc-13520843.description: PurposeInternational students navigate major academic, social, and cultural transitions while studying abroad. However, less is known about their mental health after returning home. This qualitative study explored how Algerian international student returnees understood and navigated mental health, stigma, help-seeking, and coping after returning from the United Kingdom.

pmc-13566508.title: Tobacco-Use Susceptibility and Ever-Use Categories in Relation to Depressive Symptoms Among Undergraduates at a Chinese University: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13566508.creator: Yu Chen, Xinjie Zhao, Bin Qi, Shiyu Liu, Chengbin Wu
pmc-13566508.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Depressive symptoms showed a graded cross-sectional pattern across tobacco uptake/susceptibility categories and were already elevated among ‘never users’ who lacked a firm decision not to use tobacco.Distress tracked current susceptibility rather than having tried tobacco: ‘ever users’ who remained susceptible scored 4.

pmc-13623296.title: Continuous Intravenous Acyclovir as Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy for HSV and VZV Neurological Infections: A Case Series With Pharmacokinetic and Cost Evaluation, and Review of Literature
pmc-13623296.creator: Irene G. Manders, Eline L. van Tuinen, Martijn Weisfelt, Marco Goeijenbier, Jayant S. Kalpoe, Steven F. L. van Lelyveld, Eric C. M. van Gorp, Ken Ho Hua
pmc-13623296.description: Varicella zoster virus (VZV) and herpes simplex virus (HSV) are major causes of viral meningitis and encephalitis. Standard intermittent intravenous acyclovir requires hospitalisation, reducing patient comfort and prolonging admissions. Continuous infusion may maintain therapeutic plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations while enabling treatment through Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy (OPAT).
